content: 1. A randomized controlled trial was conducted to evaluate the effectiveness of interventions among pre-clinical medical students, as published in Academic Psychiatry in 2016. 2. The World Health Organization (WHO) has consolidated guidelines addressing HIV, viral hepatitis, and sexually transmitted infections (STIs) for key populations, focusing on prevention, diagnosis, treatment, and care. These guidelines emphasize human rights, gender equality, equity, inclusion, medical ethics, universal health coverage, evidence-based public health, and community-led responses. 3. A pilot study in the United States adapted and implemented the FRESH workshop to reduce HIV-related stigma among healthcare workers, as reported in AIDS Patient Care and STDs in 2016. 4. A systematic review of interventions aimed at reducing HIV-related stigma and discrimination from 2002 to 2013 was published in the Journal of the International AIDS Society in 2013, highlighting progress and gaps in addressing stigma. 5. Research on combating HIV stigma in healthcare settings identified effective strategies, as detailed in the Journal of the International AIDS Society in 2009. 6. A systematic review published in the Journal of Multidisciplinary Healthcare in 2018 examined guidelines, tools, and best practices for reducing HIV-related stigma and discrimination in healthcare settings. 7. WHO's 2013 guidance on HIV testing, counseling, and care for adolescents living with HIV provides recommendations for a public health approach and considerations for policymakers and program managers. 8. UNAIDS released a guidance note in 2012 addressing HIV and sex work, emphasizing the importance of tailored interventions for this population. 9. A study published in PLoS One in 2014 assessed the epidemic impacts of community empowerment interventions for HIV prevention among female sex workers in both generalized and concentrated epidemics. 10. The Lancet published a 2018 article discussing the global response to HIV among sex workers and identifying unmet needs and actions. 11. A decade of technological innovation and patient empowerment in HIV testing for key populations in Europe was reviewed in HIV Medicine in 2018, highlighting the complementary role of healthcare professionals. 12. A global survey published in the Journal of Global Health Reports in 2020 emphasized the importance of community engagement and empowerment in HIV programming for key populations. 13. A literature review in the Journal of Health, Population, and Nutrition in 2006 explored the role of community empowerment in improving health outcomes. 14. A systematic review in AIDS and Behavior in 2013 demonstrated the effectiveness of community empowerment among female sex workers as an HIV prevention intervention in lowand middle-income countries. 15. Project Shikamana, a community empowerment-based HIV prevention initiative in Tanzania, significantly impacted HIV incidence and care continuum outcomes among female sex workers, as reported in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2019. 16. A Lancet article in 2015 discussed the effectiveness, challenges, and considerations for scaling up community empowerment approaches to HIV responses among sex workers. 17. A study in Current HIV/AIDS Reports in 2020 examined social determinants of HIV among female sex workers in the Dominican Republic and Tanzania, using community empowerment-based responses. 18. The Mpowerment Project, a community-building initiative for young gay and bisexual men to prevent HIV, was detailed in the American Journal of Community Psychology in 2003. 19. Research in BMC Public Health in 2021 explored family planning use among female sex workers in a community empowerment HIV prevention intervention in Tanzania, advocating for tailored programming. 20. A study in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2014 examined community responses to HIV among men who have sex with men, transgender women, female sex workers, and people who inject drugs, highlighting both benefits and potential harms. 21. A rapid review in Harm Reduction Journal in 2021 evaluated peer involvement of people who use drugs in HIV and harm reduction services in lowand middle-income countries. 22. WHO, UNAIDS, and other organizations published practical guidance in 2013 for implementing comprehensive HIV/STI programs with sex workers, emphasizing collaborative interventions. 23. A 2015 publication by the United Nations Population Fund provided guidance for implementing HIV and STI programs with men who have sex with men, focusing on collaborative approaches. 24. The United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime released a 2017 guide for implementing comprehensive HIV and HCV programs with people who inject drugs, emphasizing practical and collaborative strategies. 25. A 2016 publication by the United Nations Development Programme provided guidance for implementing HIV and STI programs with transgender people, focusing on collaborative interventions. 26. UNAIDS published a 2021 report on establishing community-led monitoring of HIV services to improve accountability and outcomes. 27. A systematic review in the Bulletin of the World Health Organization in 2018 examined violence motivated by perceptions of sexual orientation and gender identity. 28. A cross-sectional study in BMC Public Health in 2015 investigated the associations between sexual violence and health outcomes among female sex workers in The Gambia. 29. A study in Drugs: Education, Prevention, and Policy in 2020 explored the impact of extra-legal policing strategies on HIV risk among people who inject drugs in Nigeria. 30. Research in BMC Public Health in 2019 examined the intersection of intimate partner violence, depression, and sexual behavior among men who have sex with men in the PROUD trial. 31. A systematic review in Trauma, Violence, and Abuse in 2013 analyzed intimate partner violence among men who have sex with men. 32. A case study in Violence Against Women in 2020 explored the impact of violence on female sex workers in India and strategies to combat it. 33. A study in PLoS Medicine in 2017 analyzed HIV prevalence and psychosocial factors among transgender women and cisgender men who have sex with men in eight African countries. 34. Research in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2017 examined the impact of sexual violence across the lifespan on HIV risk behaviors among transgender women and cisgender people living with HIV. 35. A systematic review and meta-analysis in the American Journal of Public Health in 2020 investigated intimate partner violence in transgender populations. 36. A study in the International Journal of Drug Policy in 2019 examined police violence among people who inject drugs in Baltimore, Maryland. 37. A qualitative investigation in PLoS One in 2015 explored stigma and human rights abuses against people who inject drugs in Russia, providing insights for policy and public health strategies. 38. Research in AIDS and Behavior in 2021 examined violence, HIV risks, and polysubstance use among HIV-positive people who inject drugs in Ukraine. 39. WHO's 2004 report highlighted the effectiveness of sterile needle and syringe programs in reducing HIV/AIDS among injecting drug users. 40. WHO's 2012 guidance addressed the prevention of viral hepatitis B and C among people who inject drugs. 41. WHO's 2009 guidelines provided recommendations for the psychosocially assisted pharmacological treatment of opioid dependence. 42. WHO's 2007 report outlined interventions to address HIV in prisons, focusing on the prevention of sexual transmission. 43. WHO's 2021 consolidated guidelines addressed HIV prevention, testing, treatment, service delivery, and monitoring. 44. WHO's 2022 guidelines provided recommendations for the use of long-acting injectable cabotegravir for HIV prevention. 45. WHO's 2013 clinical and policy guidelines addressed responses to intimate partner violence and sexual violence against women. 46. WHO's guidelines for the treatment of syphilis (Treponema pallidum) were published to improve clinical outcomes.
